text:
Ana: quick Q — I'm digging into the TTFT/p99 spike we saw in prod earlier. Where's the canonical set of dashboards for TTFT, p50/p95/p99 splits, and tokens/sec by model + region? Want to tune the p95 alert but don't want to break the noise floor. :eyes:
Raj: start with Grafana -> Observability / Latency / TTFT Overview. Panels: 'TTFT by model', 'TTFT p95/p99', 'Tokens/sec (ingress)' are the skinny ones. Link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ttft/ttft-overview?orgId=1
Raj: quick PromQL for tokens/sec panel we've been using: sum(rate(tokens_ingested_total[1m])) by (model, region)
Sam: also check the 'Request path latency' dashboard for tail latency per route — useful when model routing falls back. Jaeger traces for specific requests: https://jaeger.redwood.ai/search?service=runtime&tags=%7B%7D
Sam: if you have an example trace id from the spike paste it here and I can pull it up. last time it was a regional cache miss + cold KV load.
Leo: for alert tuning, look at alert history first -> Grafana Alerts tab on the TTFT board. Our current p95 alert is: 90th? (we changed it) actually it's defined as p95(ttft_ms) > 600 for 5m. Consider switching to an adaptive window or adding a min_tokens filter to ignore tiny requests.
Leo: sample alert snippet we discussed:
```
alert: TTFT_p95_high
expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, region)) * 1000 > 600
for: 10m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/obs/ttft-playbook
```
Maya: also add a 'tokens_count' label to the alert query so we can mute very small requests. Filtering out requests < 20 tokens reduced noise for the billing team.
Maya: prefix cache hit metric helped last time — metric name: runtime_prefix_cache_hits_total. If hit rate drops then TTFT jumps for repeated prefixes.
Ana: good — thanks. Where's the panel that breaks down TTFT by phase (router / runtime / model)? I want to see if this was router queuing or model slow path.
Raj: panel 'TTFT breakdown (router/runtime/model)' on the same board. Under the hood it uses these spans: router_queue_ms, runtime_exec_ms, model_infer_ms. PromQL example:
```
sum(rate(router_queue_seconds_sum[1m])) by (model, region) / sum(rate(router_queue_seconds_count[1m])) by (model, region)
```
Sam: for traces, look for long router_queue spans then jump to runtime traces — if model_infer_ms is flat but runtime_exec_ms spikes, investigate request batching or gpu contention on Dedicated nodes.
Ana: perfect. I'm going to collect a sample trace id and a few request ids and post.
obs-bot: [ALERT] TTFT_p95_high fired for cluster-prod - region us-east-1 at 2026-03-17T14:02:44Z (alert: TTFT_p95_high) :warning:
Leo: thanks obs-bot — that's the one. From the alert runbook, start with: check prefix cache hit rate, tokens/sec by model, and top 10 traces around the firing window.
Maya: FYI, when we tuned the alert previously we added a 'noisy-model' suppression list (label: model=chatty-small) to avoid frequent alerts from spammy workloads. Might be worth re-checking that list.
Ana: ok will do. If anyone has quick pointers on where to add a temporary silence for the p95 rule (so I can experiment with thresholds without paging), ping me and I'll create it.
Raj: you can create a silence in Grafana -> Alerting -> Silence. Use tags: env=prod, alertname=TTFT_p95_high. Leave a note so oncall doesn't freak. :thumbsup:
Sam: and I'll pre-filter some traces and drop the ids here once I pull them. Thanks team.
Ana: appreciate it — will report back with trace ids + suggested new thresholds. :v:
